threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still use the bus to get to Dalston; real locals know to swap to the Overground instead for quicker connections.
Last night on the 36, I saw a guy serenading a pigeon with a ukulele. The bird just looked confused, but everyone else loved it.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I heard the spontaneous jam session in the park, a bunch of kids dancing, and someone selling homemade baklava—it hit me hard.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a Döner stand disguised as a library. Grab a kebab and a book, then sit by the canal. Unreal!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they navigate BART delays; they’ve got a backup bus route memorized and don’t even flinch at a Civic Center evacuation.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Heard a conductor over the loudspeakers asking riders to be patient while a dog took its sweet time crossing the tracks. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists love taking photos of the streets but miss the little pots of herbs outside locals' doors—it's like our secret neighborhood spice rack.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell a recent arrival by their struggle with the metro ticket machines—it's like watching a deer in headlights. Classic sign.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think it's charming that people queue for thirty minutes at the coffee shop. After a year, you'll just roll your eyes.
Last night, on the 196, a guy serenaded the bus with a ukulele while his mate tried to keep up with a karaoke app. Only in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I heard a group of kids arguing over who had the best döner in town, then politely agreeing on the same spot just around the corner.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find a kebab shop run by a former opera singer, serving döner with a side of aria. You can literally eat and hear the high notes.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s from here if they’ve memorized the BART schedule and still roll their eyes at delays, like it's a rite of passage.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Only in SF does a dog on the tracks feel like a standard Tuesday. Today’s delays were almost overshadowed by that pup’s nonchalant stroll.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the festa major is all about firecrackers, missing how locals cherish the quiet moments under the stars in Plaça del Sol.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their confusion over the metro map; they still look for the direct route instead of embracing the detours.
